solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Spanish fare preferred to Italian fare when cycling

indicators.note: cycling sends letters round from one end of the word to the other, here the last two to the front

parts.note: pasta is the classic Italian dish

explanation.surface: A diner prefers Spanish food to Italian food while out on a bike ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when cycling' moves TA from the end of PASTA to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapas are the small savoury dishes served in Spanish bars, a typical Spanish fare.

clue.text: Side perhaps putting beginnings of faith and charity after Britain in this?

indicators.note: in tells us the following letters are placed inside the word for the puzzle line itself

parts.note: this, said of the clue we are reading, means CLUE

indicators.note: after puts the three initials behind the letter for Britain
beginnings of picks the opening letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A churchy question about putting the first letters of faith and charity after Britain, as if spelling a motto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' points at the clue being read, a self-reference the solver must spot; the Britain letter and the three initials then go inside before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The face of a golf club is the striking side of its head, so 'side, perhaps' describes it by example.

clue.text: With a stake in Southern mansion, died

parts.note: a pile is a large, imposing house
d. is the standard abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone with a financial stake in a grand Southern house has died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With a stake in' looks like a financial share; it is the definition, meaning fitted with a stake.
explanation.definitionFit: A spile is a wooden stake or peg, so something spiled has had such a stake driven in.

clue.text: Army presence, could it be, spaced out in Dublin Bay?

indicators.note: spaced out means taking letters with gaps between them, here every second letter of the words

explanation.surface: A question about whether a military presence is scattered around the bay at Dublin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Army' reads as soldiers but means 'of the arm'; the answer is something present in an arm.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulna is one of the two bones of the forearm, so it is literally a presence in the arm.

clue.text: Regular users of aeroplane black box

parts.note: jet is a deep glossy black, as in jet-black
the box is slang for the television, a TV set

explanation.surface: Frequent fliers and the black box flight recorder of an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'black box' looks like the flight recorder but splits in two; 'the box' is British slang for television.
explanation.definitionFit: The jet set are wealthy people who fly about constantly between fashionable places.

clue.text: Lecturer absorbed by Twin Peaks, uplifting new plot for story

indicators.note: in a down clue, uplifting means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
absorbed by means taken inside the other piece

parts.note: two peaks: an alp, and a roof, the peak of a building

explanation.surface: A lecturer engrossed in the TV series Twin Peaks devises a new story outline.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside ROOF, giving ALP+ROOLF, which is turned upwards. 'story' is the US spelling of storey, a floor of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A floor plan is the layout drawing for one level of a building, a plot of that storey.

clue.text: Not blab about grain-store sacking on comeback campaign

indicators.note: comeback means the remaining letters run the other way
Not means the letters for blabbing are dropped from the string
about says the dropped letters sit on either side, round the outside

parts.note: a silo is a tower for storing grain
sacking a town is pillaging it
to sing is to blab to the police

explanation.surface: An instruction not to gossip about the looting of a grain store during a comeback campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: SILOPILLAGING loses S at the front and ING at the back (SING, the blab), leaving ILOPILLAG, which 'comeback' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallipoli was the ill-fated 1915-16 Allied military campaign on the Turkish peninsula of that name.

clue.text: For which a little room's needed near front of orchestra?

definitions.text: For which a little room's needed near front of orchestra?

parts.note: a cell is a small room, as in a monastery or prison

indicators.note: front of picks the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Asks which orchestral player needs a little space near the front of the orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description: the cellist sits near the front and needs elbow room.
explanation.definitionFit: Cellos are seated near the front of an orchestra, and a large bowed instrument needs room.

clue.text: At least 40 goals

definitions.meaning: a score is twenty, so two or more of them come to at least forty
points or goals made in a game

explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty, so the plural means forty or more; scores are also points or goals.

clue.text: Asian tree's great size reduced after tight squeeze

indicators.note: after places the shortened size word behind the squeeze

parts.note: a jam is a crush or tight squeeze

indicators.note: reduced means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: bulk is great size or mass

explanation.surface: An Asian tree's great size has been reduced after being crammed into a tight space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' drops the K from BULK, leaving BUL.
explanation.definitionFit: The jambul, or Java plum, is a South Asian evergreen tree grown for its purple fruit.

clue.text: Front-runner, perhaps holding off Germany, and it's gold for France!

indicators.note: holding off means keeping a letter away from the word, removing it

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
French for it's gold is c'est or

explanation.surface: A sports commentary: the front-runner holds off Germany, and France takes gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Front-runner' looks like a race leader; here it is someone who ran in front of you in time, a forebear.
explanation.definitionFit: A forebear came before, so is one who ran on ahead in the family line, a front-runner by example.

clue.text: Kermit and Emu together, in it?

indicators.note: in it says the letters sit inside the run of words before

explanation.surface: Kermit the Frog and Emu, two puppets, riding together in a two-seater.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across kermiT AND EMu; the surface pictures the two puppets on a bicycle built for two.
explanation.definitionFit: In tandem means one behind the other or working jointly, so it serves for together.

clue.text: What motorways often do during summer getaways

indicators.note: during says the letters are found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A grumble about traffic on motorways during summer holiday departures.
explanation.definitionFit: Motorways commonly join, two roads combining into one where they meet.

clue.text: 60s motoring icon after right to produce copy?

indicators.note: after puts the car name behind the letter for right

parts.note: the Jaguar E-Type was the iconic sports car of the 1960s

explanation.surface: A classic 1960s car turned up after a right turn, ready to be replicated.
explanation.walkthrough: The E-Type is the 1960s Jaguar sports car.
explanation.definitionFit: To type something again is to make a fresh copy of it.

clue.text: Priest's newly unveiled superior given a kick?

indicators.note: superior means placed above, which in a down clue is before the other piece
newly means the letters of the next word are made anew in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A priest's newly unveiled superior has been kicked.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged UNVEILED sits above (superior to) the P for priest in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink or a party given a kick has been livened up, made more stimulating.

clue.text: Career work of Kipling giving new heart to literature

indicators.note: giving new heart means the middle of the word is replaced, keeping its first and last letters

parts.note: If is the famous poem by Rudyard Kipling

explanation.surface: A literary career built on a work by Kipling that revived literature.
explanation.walkthrough: IF replaces all of LITERATURE except its outer letters L and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's life can mean their career or life's work, as in a life in the theatre.

clue.text: Contemporary poet could take a break, not mark time

indicators.note: not means the letters for mark and time are dropped

parts.note: may rest means could take a break
M is the abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A poet of today might pause for a rest, but not to mark time.
explanation.walkthrough: MAY REST loses its M and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Pam Ayres is a living English writer of comic verse, a contemporary poet.

clue.text: Take on board train an erk

indicators.note: on board means carried inside, so a letter goes into the word

parts.note: to train a gun is to aim it
R, from the Latin recipe, is the abbreviation for take used on prescriptions

explanation.surface: An instruction to get a new recruit aboard a train.
explanation.walkthrough: R is the prescription abbreviation for 'take'. Erk is British slang for a lowest-ranking member of the RAF.
explanation.definitionFit: Erk is RAF slang for an aircraftman of the lowest rank, a basic flying-service man.

clue.text: Sports club's apparently empty vessel

indicators.note: apparently, after the club, signals the club shows a nothing inside it

parts.note: a bat is the club used in cricket or baseball
empty gives O, nought or nothing

explanation.surface: A sports club's rowing vessel seems to be standing empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sports club' looks like an organisation; it is a cricket bat, holding O for 'empty'.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat is a small vessel for travelling on water.

clue.text: How much interest, so far, in censure?

indicators.note: in puts the two letters inside the word for scolding

parts.note: to berate is to censure or scold
as, in the sense of to such an extent, stands for so far, as in as far

explanation.surface: A query about how much interest there has been in a reprimand up to now.
explanation.definitionFit: The base rate is the central bank's lending rate, which sets how much interest is charged.

clue.text: Native Californian stir-fried rice's left to cool

indicators.note: stir, in stir-fried, signals the letters of fried are tossed into a new order
left means the letters for cool depart, leaving the remainder

parts.note: to ice something is to cool it

explanation.surface: Stir-fried rice is set aside to cool, a Californian cookery tip.
explanation.walkthrough: REDFI is FRIED rearranged; RICE leaves ICE ('cool') behind, giving R.
explanation.definitionFit: The red fir is a large conifer native to the mountains of California.

clue.text: Fellow, scientific expert's in sudden difficulties

indicators.note: in puts the expert inside the letters for the scientific fellow

parts.note: FRS stands for Fellow of the Royal Society, Britain's scientific academy
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A scientific fellow, an expert, finds himself in sudden trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A facer is an old term for a sudden blow or an unexpected setback faced head on.

clue.text: The last of fifty cents' change put in bag in person

indicators.note: change means the letters are reordered
The last of picks the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Fifty cents in loose change is put into a bag in person.
explanation.walkthrough: Y plus CENTS is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To encyst is to enclose in a cyst, a small sac inside the body.

clue.text: Cracking break, I want (Spain is cracking break)

indicators.note: cracking means breaking into, so letters go inside the word

parts.note: to cut is to break or sever
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A snooker player hopes for a cracking break.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket is the wordplay. 'break' in the definition is the opening shot at snooker or pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A cueist is a billiards or snooker player, who would want a good break.

clue.text: Like a game of Risk on at least two levels?

definitions.text: Like a game of Risk on at least two levels?

parts.words: Like a game of Risk on at least two levels?
parts.note: the board game Risk is played with dice, and any risk is chancy, so the word fits both ways

explanation.definitionFit: The board game Risk is played with dice, and a risky venture is chancy or uncertain.

clue.text: Front a small firm in the Home Counties?

indicators.note: in puts the article and firm inside the region

parts.note: the Home Counties, around London, lie in the south-east of England, written S EAST
CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A front company set up in the Home Counties.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties around London, in South-East England; 'Front' looks like a business cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A front is the seaside promenade or shoreline, as in seafront, where land meets the sea.

clue.text: Mediterranean port, totally restorative for vacation

indicators.note: vacation means emptying, so only the outer letters of each word remain

explanation.surface: A Mediterranean resort is wholly restorative for a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacation' looks like a holiday; it means emptying the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyre is an ancient port city on the Mediterranean coast of Lebanon.

clue.text: What picks up 5 in the real name of Magic

parts.note: the ear is what picks up sounds
V is the Roman numeral for five
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something that picks up five in the real name of a magician.
explanation.walkthrough: Magic Johnson, the US basketball star, was born Earvin Johnson.
explanation.definitionFit: The basketball player known as Magic Johnson was christened Earvin, his true first name.

clue.text: Perhaps speed will return, having swallowed a watch?

indicators.note: having swallowed means taking a letter inside
will return means the word comes back the other way

parts.note: speed is an example of a drug, amphetamine

explanation.surface: Speed reverses after a watch is swallowed.
explanation.walkthrough: DRUG turned round is GURD, which takes in A.
explanation.definitionFit: To guard is to watch over, and a watch is a guard on duty.

clue.text: Ban these sleepers playing in brass section!

indicators.note: playing means the letters are rearranged, the fodder being the brass section minus the letters of ban

explanation.surface: An instruction to stop the sleepy players in the orchestra's brass section.
explanation.walkthrough: BAN plus the answer ('these') rearranged gives BRASS SECTION, so the answer is BRASS SECTION with BAN removed, reshuffled. Railway sleepers are crossties in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossties is the American term for railway sleepers, the beams that support the rails.
